text:
kevin: Quick heads-up — saw a regression on host-side tokenization latency during the 03:00 load window. Correlates with KV cache eviction storms + lots of tiny streaming chunks. Putting raw traces here for visibility. :eyes:

maria: Ugh, that combo rings a bell. Any flamegraphs or perf recordings?

kevin: Uploaded a pprof capture to the usual spot: https://telemetry/redwood/pprof/4751234567 (check cpu flame). Top of stack is tokenize_sync -> parse_request -> http2_frame_handler.

lee: Can you paste the short flame snippet? I want to see if tokenize_sync is on the main epoll loop.

kevin: Sure — simplified stack sample from the flame: 
```
http2_frame_handler
  parse_headers
  parse_body
  tokenize_sync
    bpe_encode
    normalizer::run
kernel_selector::select_for_seq_len
```
Tokenize is synchronous and blocking the frame handler when frames are many small chunks (~200B).

jen: How small are the chunks? Is this mostly gRPC streaming or HTTP/1.1 chunked?

kevin: Mostly HTTP/2 streaming (ingress->host proxy) with HPACK overhead. Client sends many small partial frames (avg ~180B). That plus KV cache eviction spikes (hot shard) causes CPU thrashing — eviction callbacks create brief GC-ish pauses and increase syscall counts -> context switches.

derek: Do we have metrics showing syscall rates? evictions per sec?

kevin: Yes — cpu_sys increased 3x and context_switches spiked inline with eviction_rate ~ 120/s on the hot shard. KV cache reported 98% occupancy, then evict bursts when memory pressure hit.

maria: Hypothesis: synchronous tokenization on ingress amplifies small-frame overhead. Options: 1) pre-tokenize in sidecar worker pool (async), 2) coalesce small frames earlier in the proxy, 3) lightweight fast-path tokenization (no normalizer) for the short prefix then background normalize.

lee: Also kernel selection: we're running kernel_selector per request and it queries sequence-length histogram which is hot and contended when many tiny sequences arrive. Maybe cache kernel decisions for short sequences to avoid hotspot.

jen: Good catch. Micro-benchmark: for <=32 tokens, fused_short_kernel is ~20% faster and cheaper to pick. We can memoize key=(model,quant,seq_bucket)->kernel for 1s.

kevin: I prototyped two changes locally: move tokenize_sync to a small worker pool (4 threads) and add an early coalesce in acceptor to join frames up to 1KB or 10ms. Quick numbers from a replay: p95 tokenization latency down from 12ms->5ms, overall request p95 down 18%. CPU sys drops ~25%.

derek: Nice. Any regressions or concurrency hazards from the worker pool? Race with KV cache callbacks?

kevin: Need to be careful: tokenization now sees requests after we've done header parsing. So we still hold ownership of request buffers. I used a copy-to-worker (fast memcpy) to avoid touching shared buffer later. There is a small alloc spike but overall cheaper than stalling main loop.

lee: For kernel memoization I sketched this patch: 
```
// simple 1s memo for short seqs
struct KernelCache { map<string, (kernel_id, expiry)> cache; }
if (seq_len <= 32) {
  auto k = cache.lookup(key);
  if (k && k.expiry > now) use(k.kernel_id);
  else { k = compute_kernel(); cache.insert(key, {k, now+1s}); }
}
```
Should be lock-free per-shard with atomic pointer swap to avoid contention.

maria: Actionable plan:
- canary the worker-pool tokenization behind a flag on a dedicated hostpool (kevin)
- add 1s kernel memo layer on short seqs (lee)
- add 1KB/10ms coalesce in ingress proxy (jen)
- short-term: increase KV cache hot-shard limit + smoother eviction policy to reduce bursts (derek)

jen: Also add a telemetry tag to correlate tokenization time with eviction_rate and small_frame_ratio so we can dashboard post-rollout.

kevin: I'll submit the tokenization canary PR later today. Basic diff: 
```
+ // offload tokenize to small pool
+ if (FLAGS.tokenize_async) {
+   buf_copy = buffer.clone_small();
+   tokenize_pool.enqueue([buf_copy, ctx]{ tokenize(buf_copy); ctx.resume(); });
+ } else {
+   tokenize_sync(buf);
+ }
```
Benchmark harness: replay recorded traces with 2k qps, 60/40 small/large frames mix.

lee: I'll land kernel cache patch in a small PR and add per-shard atomic slot. Will include microbench numbers.

derek: For KV side, I'll tune LRU thresholds and add a jittered eviction window to avoid synchronous bursts. Will coordinate with infra to bump the hot-shard memory soft-limit a bit for the canary hosts.

maria: Cool. Rollout plan: canary 10 hosts for 2h with traffic shaping, then 100 hosts 24h, watch p95 tokenization, p999 overall, cpu_sys, ctx_switch. If telemetry shows reversion we rollback.

kevin: @jen can you add the dashboard tags and an alert for tokenization p95 > 10ms?

jen: On it. Also adding small-frame-ratio and eviction_rate panels.

sre-bot: Deploy-canary queued for hostpool "ingress-canary-2" by kevin. Link: https://deploys/1234

kevin: Thanks. Will post PR links and initial canary numbers in this thread when done. :thumbsup:
